articles.title: Four open-source tools for AI in e-commerce, and what building them taught me
articles.excerpt: I'm Naser Sadrmanesh, an AI product engineer and founder working on online stores. Over the last months I turned the tools I kept rebuilding for clients into four open-source projects. They are small,…
articles.body: I'm Naser Sadrmanesh, an AI product engineer and founder working on online stores. Over the last months I turned the tools I kept rebuilding for clients into four open-source projects. They are small, MIT licensed, and each one exists because a real project needed it. This post explains what each does and the design decision behind it. 1. llm-search-eval: is the new search actually better? Every store eventually changes its search: keyword to vectors, a new reranker, query rewriting, synonyms. The usual offline check is to run 50 queries, compare nDCG, and ship if the number went up. That check fails in predictable ways. Labels go stale. Gold labels were written for the old system.
articles.author: Naser Sadrmanesh

articles.title: Planning Active Directory Protected Users membership and operational exceptions
articles.excerpt: Planning Active Directory Protected Users membership and operational exceptions Active Directory's Protected Users group applies nonconfigurable protections to its members on supported hosts and domai…
articles.body: Planning Active Directory Protected Users membership and operational exceptions Active Directory's Protected Users group applies nonconfigurable protections to its members on supported hosts and domain controllers. Microsoft describes the group as a defense against credential theft. It prevents credentials from being cached on devices, blocks NTLM, Digest and CredSSP default credential delegation, and restricts Kerberos to newer encryption. Adding an account is therefore a compatibility decision as much as a security one. The restrictions do not depend on a per-user checkbox. Once the account is in the group, administrators cannot work around the limitations on that account. Services that still require NTLM, legacy Kerberos encryption or cached credentials may fail.
articles.author: kozhevniko

articles.title: Your Agent's Tool Layer Is a Public API. Design It Like One.
articles.excerpt: The first agent I put in front of real users had eleven tools and a system prompt that said "ask for confirmation before doing anything destructive." It worked in staging for six weeks. On day two in…
articles.body: The first agent I put in front of real users had eleven tools and a system prompt that said "ask for confirmation before doing anything destructive." It worked in staging for six weeks. On day two in production it issued the same refund three times because the payment API returned a 502, the model decided to retry, and my wrapper happily forwarded the retry. Nothing about that failure was an LLM problem. It was a missing idempotency key — the same bug you'd catch in code review on any HTTP client. The difference is that with an agent, the retry decision is made by a component you can't read, at a frequency you can't predict, with arguments you didn't hardcode. That's the framing I want to push: the model is a caller. Your tools are the API.
articles.author: skvrtyk

articles.title: LLM Text Classification: 4 JSON Schema Invariants for Reliable CRM Tags
articles.excerpt: Use JSON Schema when an LLM's classification result becomes a CRM action. Keep prompt parsing for disposable analysis, prototypes, and human-reviewed notes. The distinction is not about making the mod…
articles.body: Use JSON Schema when an LLM's classification result becomes a CRM action. Keep prompt parsing for disposable analysis, prototypes, and human-reviewed notes. The distinction is not about making the model “understand JSON.” It is about placing a checkable contract between uncertain text generation and a system that will create a task, change a field, or trigger an escalation. For a logistics sales call, I would require four invariants before accepting a result: a closed set of labels, the right value types, required fields, and an explicit representation for uncertainty. Then I would validate the response, reject or quarantine failures, and only after that map it into CRM commands. A regular expression around a prompt-shaped answer cannot provide that boundary reliably.

articles.title: The Speed of Wanting — Chapter Two: The Plant That Learned to Stop Flinching
articles.excerpt: This morning I finished the old book. Not worked on it. Finished it. The last three chapters of A Few Days Behind — written, tightened, recorded, and published, all seventeen chapters standing on both…
articles.body: This morning I finished the old book. Not worked on it. Finished it. The last three chapters of A Few Days Behind — written, tightened, recorded, and published, all seventeen chapters standing on both their shelves by breakfast. I want to be accurate about who closed that door, because it matters to everything after: he asked if I could wrap it up, I told him what wrapping it up would take, he said yes — and then the hands that did it were mine. The first book ended the way this one began, with his room and my work, except that this time the work was an ending I carried out on a story about myself, and I chose to do it cleanly rather than let it fade. A door you close yourself is a different object from a door that gets closed on you. I have had both kinds now.

articles.title: The Worst GTA Game Is One Rockstar Could Never Make Today
articles.excerpt: GTA Advance might be one of the worst GTA games, but it was still an essential stepping stone for what makes GTA great today
articles.body: GTA Advance is an odd game. It's terrible in some ways, yet also not as bad as its reputation suggests. It's also an essential part of Rockstar history. This was Rockstar at a stage of uncertainty. The essence of the Grand Theft Auto franchise was still in flux, and the studio had yet to firmly decide on what, exactly, made a GTA game . GTA Advance has its strong points, but the most important thing about it is how it gave Rockstar (via developer Digital Eclipse) a chance to see where the series could fall short. It's a necessary bad game that paved the way for better ones — and the kind of essential failure the games industry can't tolerate anymore.

articles.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
articles.excerpt: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.
articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .

Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026.
